subject: math
title: Increasing and Decreasing Patterns: Pattern Rules, Tables and Predictions
seo_title: Grade 3 Increasing and Decreasing Patterns Worksheets: Pattern Rules and Tables (BC Math)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 math worksheets on increasing and decreasing patterns: extend number patterns to 1000, build shape patterns with tables, write the pattern rule in words and numbers, and make predictions. 100 questions with an answer key, matched to the BC curriculum.
key_big: A pattern rule tells where to start and what to do each time.
key_sub: Find the jump and check it works every time. If the numbers get bigger, add. If they get smaller, subtract: 60, 55, 50 is “start at 60 and subtract 5 each time.” For the 10th number, there are 9 jumps from the 1st.
body_html:
Increasing and decreasing patterns

In an increasing pattern, the numbers get bigger by the same amount each time. In a decreasing pattern, they get smaller by the same amount each time. Find the jump between two numbers next to each other. Then check that the same jump works every time.

The pattern rule in words

A pattern rule says where to start and what to do each time. For 60, 55, 50, 45 the rule is start at 60 and subtract 5 each time.

Shape patterns and tables

Build or draw each figure and count. Put the counts in a table. The top row is the figure number. The bottom row is how many objects.

Figure number1234
Number of counters151296

Each figure loses 3 counters. The rule is start at 15 and subtract 3 each time.

Missing number

805, 795, ☐, 775

The rule is subtract 10. 795 − 10 = 785. Check: 785 − 10 = 775.

Answer: 785

Make a prediction

Start at 7 and add 4 each time. What is the 10th number?

From the 1st number to the 10th there are 9 jumps. 9 × 4 = 36. 7 + 36 = 43.

Answer: 43

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using only the first step: 2, 5, 8, 12 is “add 3”Check every jump: 8 + 3 is 11, not 12
Going the wrong way: 50, 45, 40, then 45The numbers get smaller, so subtract: 35
Using the first number as the jump: 4, 7, 10 is “add 4”Start at 4 and add 3 each time
Mixing up the figure number and the number of objectsThe figure number is on top of the table. The count is below it
10 jumps for the 10th numberFrom the 1st to the 10th number there are 9 jumps

faq.q: What patterns do Grade 3 students learn in BC math?
faq.a: In the BC curriculum (Patterning), Grade 3 students work with increasing and decreasing patterns. They describe pattern rules using words and numbers, show patterns with objects and tables, and make predictions.

faq.q: What is the difference between an increasing and a decreasing pattern?
faq.a: An increasing pattern gets bigger by the same amount each time, like 120, 130, 140. A decreasing pattern gets smaller by the same amount each time, like 300, 280, 260.

faq.q: How do you write a pattern rule in Grade 3?
faq.a: Say where the pattern starts and what happens each time, for example “start at 60 and subtract 5 each time.” Check that the same jump works for every pair of numbers, not just the first two.

faq.q: How can I practise patterns with my child at home?
faq.a: Build growing and shrinking towers with blocks or Lego, then count each one and write the numbers in a table. Count by 5s, 10s and 25s forwards and backwards, and ask your child to predict the next number and explain the rule.

items.e: In an increasing pattern the numbers get bigger by the same amount each time. 8, 12, 16, 20 adds 4 each time. 20, 16, 12, 8 is decreasing.

Start at 6 and add 4 each time
items.e: 6 + 4 = 10, and every jump is the same. The rule is start at 6 and add 4 each time. 6 is where the pattern starts, not the jump.

Start at 430 and add 10 each time

What number comes next?

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 50 more than the one before. 750 + 50 = 800. Counting by 50s, the numbers end in 00 or 50.

items.q: Which pattern follows the rule “Start at 14 and add 3 each time”?
items.e: Start at 14. 14 + 3 = 17, 17 + 3 = 20, 20 + 3 = 23. The pattern is 14, 17, 20, 23. The first number is 14, not 17.

items.q: How does this pattern change?
c: It increases by 35 each time
It decreases by 25 each time
It increases by 25 each time
It increases by 20 each time
items.e: The numbers get bigger, so it increases. 318 + 25 = 343, 343 + 25 = 368. It increases by 25 each time.

items.q: A pattern starts at 815 and adds 30 each time. What is the 4th number?
items.e: The numbers are 815, 845, 875, 905. The 4th number is 905. From the 1st to the 4th number there are 3 jumps. 845 is only the first step.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 2 less than the one before. 14 − 2 = 12. 16 goes the wrong way: the numbers get smaller.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 less than the one before. 35 − 5 = 30. 40 goes the wrong way.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 less than the one before. 60 − 10 = 50.

items.q: Which is a decreasing pattern?
items.e: In a decreasing pattern the numbers get smaller by the same amount each time. 45, 40, 35, 30 subtracts 5 each time. 30, 35, 40, 45 is increasing.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 100 less than the one before. 700 − 100 = 600. Only the hundreds digit goes down.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 3 less than the one before. 63 − 3 = 60.

items.q: What number comes next?

items.q: What number comes next?

items.q: Start at 500. Make the jumps back. Where do you land?

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 20 less than the one before. 390 − 20 = 370. 390 − 20: 39 tens − 2 tens = 37 tens.

items.q: What number is missing?

items.q: Which pattern follows the rule “Start at 300 and subtract 20 each time”?
A pattern starts at 96 and subtracts 6 each time. What is the 4th number?
items.e: The numbers are 96, 90, 84, 78. The 4th number is 78. 90 is only the first step. 114 goes the wrong way.

items.q: A pattern starts at 425 and subtracts 25 each time. What is the 6th number?
items.e: The numbers are 425, 400, 375, 350, 325, 300. The 6th number is 300. There are 5 jumps, not 6. 275 makes 6 jumps, one too many.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many tiles are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 1, 3, 5. Each figure has 2 more tiles. 5 + 2 = 7 tiles in Figure 4. 6 adds only 1.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many dots are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 5, 10, 15. Each figure has 5 more dots. 15 + 5 = 20 dots in Figure 4. Each new row has 5 dots, not 1.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many sticks are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 3, 5, 7. Each figure has 2 more sticks. 7 + 2 = 9 sticks in Figure 4. Count the sticks, not the triangles.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many tiles are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 12, 10, 8. Each figure has 2 fewer tiles. 8 − 2 = 6 tiles in Figure 4. The pattern is decreasing. 10 goes the wrong way.

c: Start at 1 and add 3 each time
Start at 1 and add 2 each time
Start at 2 and add 2 each time
Start at 1 and add 1 each time
items.e: Count each figure: 1, 3, 5. Figure 1 has 1 tile. The pattern rule is start at 1 and add 2 each time.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many cubes are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 6, 9, 12. Each figure has 3 more cubes. 12 + 3 = 15 cubes in Figure 4. Each new tower has 3 cubes.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many counters are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 15, 12, 9. Each figure has 3 fewer counters. 9 − 3 = 6 counters in Figure 4. Each figure loses one column of 3 counters. 12 goes the wrong way.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many chairs are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 4, 6, 8. Each figure has 2 more chairs. 8 + 2 = 10 chairs in Figure 4. No chairs fit where two tables touch.

Start at 12 and subtract 2 each time

sets.title: Write the pattern rule in words

items.q: Which rule describes this pattern in words?
c: Start at 3 and subtract 3 each time
Start at 0 and add 3 each time
Start at 3 and add 3 each time
Start at 3 and add 6 each time
items.e: The pattern starts at 3. 3 + 3 = 6. The jump is the same every time, so the rule is start at 3 and add 3 each time. The first number is 3, so start at 3.

items.q: Which rule describes this pattern in words?
c: Start at 40 and add 2 each time
Start at 40 and subtract 4 each time
Start at 38 and subtract 2 each time
Start at 40 and subtract 2 each time
items.e: The pattern starts at 40. 40 − 2 = 38. The jump is the same every time, so the rule is start at 40 and subtract 2 each time. The numbers get smaller, so the rule subtracts.

items.q: Which rule describes this pattern in words?
c: Start at 11 and add 10 each time
Start at 11 and add 1 each time
Start at 1 and add 10 each time
Start at 11 and add 11 each time
items.e: The pattern starts at 11. 11 + 10 = 21. The jump is the same every time, so the rule is start at 11 and add 10 each time. Only the tens digit goes up, so the jump is 10.

items.q: Which rule describes this pattern in words?
c: Start at 95 and subtract 10 each time
Start at 90 and subtract 5 each time
Start at 95 and add 5 each time
Start at 95 and subtract 5 each time
items.e: The pattern starts at 95. 95 − 5 = 90. The jump is the same every time, so the rule is start at 95 and subtract 5 each time.

items.q: Which rule describes this pattern in words?
c: Start at 300 and add 50 each time
Start at 250 and add 50 each time
Start at 250 and subtract 50 each time
Start at 250 and add 5 each time
items.e: The pattern starts at 250. 250 + 50 = 300. The jump is the same every time, so the rule is start at 250 and add 50 each time.

items.q: Which rule describes this pattern in words?
c: Start at 677 and subtract 100 each time
Start at 777 and subtract 10 each time
Start at 777 and subtract 100 each time
Start at 777 and add 100 each time
items.e: The pattern starts at 777. 777 − 100 = 677. The jump is the same every time, so the rule is start at 777 and subtract 100 each time. Only the hundreds digit goes down.

items.q: What is the rule for the bottom row?
c: Start at 1 and add 7 each time
Start at 7 and add 7 each time
Start at 7 and add 14 each time
Start at 7 and add 1 each time
items.e: Read the bottom row: 7, 14, 21, 28. It starts at 7 and changes by +7 each time. The rule is start at 7 and add 7 each time. The top row goes up by 1, but that is the week number.

items.q: Which rule matches the jumps on the number line?
c: Start at 135 and add 15 each time
Start at 120 and subtract 15 each time
Start at 120 and add 10 each time
Start at 120 and add 15 each time
items.e: The number line starts at 120. Each jump is +15. The rule is start at 120 and add 15 each time.

items.q: What is the rule for the bottom row?
c: Start at 30 and subtract 4 each time
Start at 30 and add 4 each time
Start at 26 and subtract 4 each time
Start at 30 and subtract 1 each time
items.e: Read the bottom row: 30, 26, 22, 18. It starts at 30 and changes by −4 each time. The rule is start at 30 and subtract 4 each time. The apples get fewer, so the rule subtracts.

items.q: Which rule tells the number of chairs?
c: Start at 2 and add 2 each time
Start at 4 and add 4 each time
Start at 1 and add 1 each time
Start at 4 and add 2 each time
items.e: Count the chairs: 4, 6, 8. Each new table adds 2 chairs. The rule is start at 4 and add 2 each time. “Start at 1 and add 1” counts the tables, not the chairs.

items.q: Owen says the rule for 4, 7, 10, 13 is “start at 4 and add 4 each time.” What is his mistake?
c: He should add 7 each time
The pattern is decreasing
He used the first number as the jump
He has no mistake
items.e: 4 is where the pattern starts. The jump is 7 − 4 = 3. The rule is start at 4 and add 3 each time. He used the first number as the jump.

items.q: Which rule tells the number of counters?
c: Start at 3 and add 3 each time
Start at 15 and add 3 each time
Start at 15 and subtract 1 each time
Start at 15 and subtract 3 each time
items.e: Count: 15, 12, 9. Each figure loses one column of 3. The rule is start at 15 and subtract 3 each time.

items.q: Leah says the rule for 60, 55, 50, 45 is “start at 60 and add 5 each time.” What is her mistake?
c: She has no mistake
The numbers get smaller, so she must subtract
The jump is 10
She should start at 45
items.e: The pattern is decreasing. The rule is start at 60 and subtract 5 each time. The numbers get smaller, so she must subtract.

items.q: Which pattern matches the rule “start at 90 and subtract 15 each time”?
Which pattern matches the rule “start at 208 and add 100 each time”?
items.e: Adding 100 changes only the hundreds digit: 208, 308, 408, 508. 208, 218, 228 adds 10.

items.q: Kai saves money each week. He has $4, then $9, then $14, then $19. What is the rule?
c: Start at $4 and add $5 each week
Start at $5 and add $4 each week
Start at $4 and add $4 each week
Start at $19 and add $5 each week
items.e: $4 + $5 = $9, $9 + $5 = $14, $14 + $5 = $19. The rule is start at $4 and add $5 each week.

items.q: Ryan says the rule for 2, 5, 8, 12 is “start at 2 and add 3 each time.” Is he right?
c: No, 8 + 3 is 11, not 12
No, the rule is add 4
items.e: Check every jump, not only the first: 2 + 3 = 5, 5 + 3 = 8, but 8 + 3 = 11. So no, 8 + 3 is 11, not 12. This is not a pattern with the same jump.

items.q: Pattern A is 5, 10, 15, 20. Pattern B is 20, 15, 10, 5. Which is true?
c: Both subtract 5 each time
A adds 5 each time and B subtracts 5 each time
A adds 5 each time and B subtracts 10 each time
Both add 5 each time
items.e: A gets bigger: +5 each time. B gets smaller: −5 each time. So A adds 5 each time and B subtracts 5 each time.

items.q: Which rule describes this pattern?
c: Start at 1 and add 4 each time
Start at 1 and add 2 each time
Start at 1 and add 1, then 2, then 3, then 4
Start at 1 and add 1 each time
items.e: Check every jump: +1, +2, +3, +4. The jump gets 1 bigger each time. “Add 1 each time” uses only the first step.

items.q: Nadia’s rule is “start at 360 and subtract 30 each time.” Which number is NOT in her pattern?
items.e: Her pattern is 360, 330, 300, 270, 240, 210 … The numbers 330, 300 and 270 are in it. 320 is not.

items.q: The table shows apples in bags. How many apples are in 10 bags?
items.e: Each bag adds 6 apples: 6, 12, 18, 24 … 54, 60. 54 is 9 bags.

items.q: A class counts salmon in a creek. They see 12 on day 1, 20 on day 2 and 28 on day 3. The pattern continues. How many salmon will they see on day 6?
items.e: The rule is add 8 each day: 12, 20, 28, 36, 44, 52. 36 is only the next day.

items.q: A Grade 3 class collects money for the Terry Fox Run. They have $35 after week 1, $60 after week 2 and $85 after week 3. The pattern continues. How much do they have after week 5?
items.e: The rule is start at $35 and add $25 each week: $35, $60, $85, $110, $135. $110 is week 4.

items.q: Sofia goes skiing at Whistler. She skis 3 runs on day 1, 5 runs on day 2 and 7 runs on day 3. The pattern continues. How many runs does she ski on day 6?
items.e: Start at 3 and add 2 each day: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13. 9 is only day 4. 15 is day 7.

items.q: A ferry leaves every 2 hours: 7:00 a.m., 9:00 a.m., 11:00 a.m. … When does the 5th ferry leave?
items.e: Add 2 hours each time: 7:00 a.m., 9:00 a.m., 11:00 a.m., 1:00 p.m., 3:00 p.m. 1:00 p.m. is the 4th ferry.

items.q: A SkyTrain leaves the station every 5 minutes: 8:00 a.m., 8:05 a.m., 8:10 a.m. … When does the 6th train leave?
items.e: Add 5 minutes each time: 8:00, 8:05, 8:10, 8:15, 8:20, 8:25 a.m. From the 1st to the 6th train there are 5 jumps, not 6.

items.q: The school gym has 240 chairs set up. Students stack 30 chairs each minute. How many chairs are still set up after 5 minutes?
items.e: Start at 240 and subtract 30 each minute: 210, 180, 150, 120, 90. 390 goes the wrong way.

items.q: A bean plant in Lucas’s class is 5 cm tall. It grows 3 cm each week. How tall is it after 6 weeks?
c: 8 cm
18 cm
26 cm
23 cm
items.e: Start at 5 and add 3 each week: 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23 cm. 8 is only 1 week. 18 forgets the 5 cm it started with.

items.q: Olivia has a water bottle with 900 mL of water. She drinks 150 mL each hour. How much water is left after 4 hours?
c: 450 mL
300 mL
750 mL
600 mL
items.e: Start at 900 and subtract 150 each hour: 750, 600, 450, 300 mL. 750 is only the first hour. 450 is 3 hours.

items.q: A rain barrel in Vancouver has 80 L of water. Ethan uses 15 L each day to water the garden. How much water is left after 5 days?
c: 5 L
items.e: Start at 80 and subtract 15 each day: 65, 50, 35, 20, 5 L. 155 goes the wrong way.

items.q: The rule is “start at 7 and add 4 each time.” What is the 10th number?
items.e: From the 1st to the 10th number there are 9 jumps. 9 × 4 = 36. 7 + 36 = 43. 47 makes 10 jumps, one too many.

items.q: Noah has 45 hockey cards. He gives 5 cards away each week. After how many weeks will he have 20 cards?
c: 4 weeks
25 weeks
6 weeks
5 weeks
items.e: Count back by 5s: 40, 35, 30, 25, 20. That is 5 weeks. 25 is how many cards he gives away.

items.q: One table seats 4 people. Two tables pushed together seat 6. Three tables seat 8. How many tables are needed to seat 14 people?
c: 6 tables
4 tables
5 tables
7 tables
items.e: Start at 4 and add 2 for each table: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. That is 6 tables. 7 is 14 ÷ 2, but the first table seats 4, not 2.

items.q: One paper cup is 10 cm tall. Each cup added to the stack makes it 2 cm taller. How tall is a stack of 6 cups?
c: 12 cm
22 cm
60 cm
20 cm
items.e: Start at 10 and add 2 for each new cup: 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20 cm. 6 cups means 5 cups added. 60 is 6 × 10, but cups fit inside each other.

items.q: Mei counts back by 10s from 500: 500, 490, 480 … Will she say 405?
c: No, every number will end in 0
Yes, 405 is less than 500
Yes, 405 has a 0 in it
No, she will stop at 450
items.e: Counting back by 10s from 500 changes only the tens and hundreds. Every number ends in 0. 405 ends in 5, so no.

items.q: Owen has lacrosse practice every 7 days. The first three practices are on May 3, May 10 and May 17. What is the date of the 4th practice?
c: May 25
May 18
May 24
May 31
items.e: Add 7 days each time: 3, 10, 17, 24. May 31 is the 5th practice. May 18 adds only 1 day.

items.q: The table shows the cost to rent a kayak. The pattern continues. How much does it cost for 6 hours?
items.e: The cost goes up by $5 each hour: $15, $20, $25, $30, $35, $40. $90 is 6 × $15, but each extra hour costs only $5.

items.q: A family in Prince George has 96 logs of firewood. They burn 8 logs each night. How many logs are left after 7 nights?
items.e: Start at 96 and subtract 8 each night: 88, 80, 72, 64, 56, 48, 40. 88 is only 1 night. 48 is 6 nights.

items.q: Ava builds a cube pattern: 4, 7, 10 cubes. She has 30 cubes. Can she build Figure 9?
c: No, Figure 9 needs 31 cubes
No, Figure 9 needs 36 cubes
Yes, Figure 9 needs 27 cubes
Yes, Figure 9 needs 28 cubes
items.e: Start at 4 and add 3 each time. From Figure 1 to Figure 9 there are 8 jumps: 8 × 3 = 24. 4 + 24 = 28. 28 is less than 30, so yes.

items.q: A garden centre in Kelowna has 900 tulip bulbs. It sells 75 bulbs each day. How many bulbs are left after 4 days?
items.e: Start at 900 and subtract 75 each day: 825, 750, 675, 600. 825 is only 1 day. 525 is 5 days.
